title: Agent Framework built-in telemetry
summary: Agent Framework emits OpenTelemetry spans and metrics for agent runs, model calls and tool calls. You supply the exporter. Python instrumentation is on by default since python-1.6.0, .NET needs a wrapper, and sensitive content stays off unless you enable it.
useIf: You build agents or workflows with Agent Framework and want traces and metrics in any OpenTelemetry backend.
avoidIf: You assume telemetry flows by default: spans are created, but no exporter is installed automatically.

explain.md: The framework follows the OTel GenAI conventions. Spans: `invoke_agent <agent_name>` at the top, `chat <model_name>` per model call and `execute_tool <function_name>` per tool. Metrics: `gen_ai.client.operation.duration` (histogram, seconds), `gen_ai.client.token.usage` (histogram, tokens) and `agent_framework.function.invocation.duration` (histogram, seconds). Workflows add `workflow.build`, `workflow.session` (.NET and Go) or `workflow.run` (Python), `workflow_invoke`, `executor.process {executor_id}`, `edge_group.process` and `message.send`. The docs' sample trace is dated 2025-09-25 and predates the current convention names, and which build emits which attribute and metric names is UNVERIFIED [[r10]] [[r11]].

blocks.md: `configure_otel_providers()` reads the standard `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*` variables, or set `ENABLE_CONSOLE_EXPORTERS=true`. You can also pass your own exporters, or configure your own SDK and call `enable_instrumentation(enable_sensitive_data=False)`. Instrumentation became on by default in python-1.6.0 (2026-05-21), but no exporter is installed automatically [[r10]] [[tr6]].

blocks.title: Environment variables from the docs (defaults in comments)
blocks.code:
ENABLE_INSTRUMENTATION=true          # default true
ENABLE_SENSITIVE_DATA=false          # default false
ENABLE_CONSOLE_EXPORTERS=false       # default false
OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=support-agent      # default agent_framework
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=grpc     # docs list grpc or http, default grpc
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:4317

blocks.md: Wrap the chat client or the agent with `.AsBuilder().UseOpenTelemetry(sourceName, cfg => cfg.EnableSensitiveData = ...)`. The default source name is `Experimental.Microsoft.Agents.AI`, and the tracer and meter providers must call `AddSource` with the same name. Instrumenting both layers duplicates prompts and responses when sensitive data is on, so pick one. The Harness wraps both layers by default (`OpenTelemetrySourceName`, `DisableOpenTelemetry`) [[r10]].

explain.md: **Sensitive data** means prompts, responses, tool arguments and tool results, and it is off by default. Turn instrumentation off with `ENABLE_INSTRUMENTATION=false`, `enable_instrumentation=False` on the agent or `disable_instrumentation()`. For local work, run the standalone Aspire Dashboard in Docker, set `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:4317` and open `http://localhost:18888` [[r10]].

explain.title: MCP context only for sessions the agent opens
explain.md: In Python the framework injects W3C trace context into `params._meta` for `MCPStreamableHTTPTool`, `MCPStdioTool` and `MCPWebsocketTool` sessions it opens itself, not for hosted or provider-managed MCP tools. .NET behavior is UNVERIFIED because the docs describe it for Python only [[r10]].

whereToUse: Local development with the Aspire Dashboard to see agent, model and tool spans
Production export to Application Insights, Langfuse, LangSmith, Phoenix or any OTLP endpoint
Workflow debugging with executor and edge spans
Cost dashboards from the framework's duration and token metrics
Teams that must keep content off spans by default

use: Configure an exporter explicitly, because the framework does not install one
Leave `ENABLE_SENSITIVE_DATA` false in production and capture content through a governed path
Instrument one layer in .NET, and let the Harness do both only when you use it
avoid: Do not assume spans reach a backend because instrumentation is on by default
Do not point the default gRPC exporter at a backend that accepts only OTLP over HTTP
Do not build dashboards on metric names you have not seen in your backend
flips: The backend accepts only HTTP OTLP (for example Langfuse): set the protocol to http
You run through Foundry hosted agents: use Foundry server-side tracing for the hosted part and framework telemetry for your own code
Telemetry overhead is a concern: disable it for hot paths or sample traces and keep metrics

pitfalls.symptom: Nothing arrives in the backend even though instrumentation is on
pitfalls.cause: Spans are created by default, but no exporter is configured
pitfalls.fix: Set `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*`, enable console exporters for a check, or pass exporters in code [[r10]]

pitfalls.symptom: Langfuse shows nothing from a default Python agent
pitfalls.cause: The framework's default OTLP protocol is gRPC and Langfuse accepts only OTLP over HTTP (HTTP/JSON or HTTP/protobuf)
pitfalls.fix: Set the protocol to http and use the `/api/public/otel` endpoint with the required headers [[r17]]

pitfalls.cause: Both the chat client and the agent were wrapped with sensitive data on

scenarios.title: A laptop workflow with a new agent
scenarios.situation: A developer builds an agent with Agent Framework and wants to see spans and token counts while iterating. Data is synthetic and the machine has Docker.
unknowns: Is the developer behind a proxy that blocks local ports?
scenarios.question: How do you view telemetry?

options.name: Run the Aspire Dashboard in Docker and point the OTLP endpoint at localhost:4317
options.why: It shows traces, logs and metrics locally with no cloud setup.
options.tradeoff: Local only, so it does not replace a production backend.

options.name: Console exporters
options.tradeoff: Hard to read nested spans in a terminal.

options.name: Export straight to the production backend with sensitive data on
options.why: Development prompts mix into production telemetry and may expose test data.
options.tradeoff: Fine only for a dedicated dev project in the backend.

flips.then: Use console exporters or a hosted dev project.
Use a shared dev backend with restricted access.

scenarios.takeaway: Use a local viewer while iterating and keep content on only there.

scenarios.title: Sending Agent Framework traces to Langfuse
scenarios.situation: A team wants Agent Framework Python traces in Langfuse for prompt and eval tooling. The first attempt produced no data.
constraints: Backend accepts OTLP over HTTP only
scenarios.question: What is the fix?

options.name: Set the OTLP protocol to http, use the Langfuse `/api/public/otel` endpoint and its auth header
options.why: It matches what Langfuse accepts: OTLP over HTTP, not gRPC.
options.tradeoff: This follows from the two docs pages, not from a vendor statement, so verify with a test span.

options.name: Run an OpenTelemetry Collector that receives gRPC and exports HTTP to Langfuse
options.why: Works with the default exporter and gives you tail sampling too.

options.name: Keep gRPC and point it at Langfuse
options.why: Langfuse does not support gRPC, so exports fail.
options.tradeoff: Right for backends that accept gRPC OTLP.

flips.then: Send gRPC to it and let it export HTTP.

flips.if: Content must stay out of Langfuse
flips.then: Keep `ENABLE_SENSITIVE_DATA` false and check what the attributes hold.

scenarios.takeaway: Match the exporter protocol to the backend.

quiz.q: Python instrumentation is on by default, yet no data reaches the backend. Why?
options: No exporter is installed automatically, so spans are created but not exported
Instrumentation turns off after one hour
The framework only exports to Application Insights
Sensitive data must be on to export anything
quiz.explain: Spans are created but nothing is exported until you configure an exporter. The framework is backend-neutral and the sensitive-data flag only controls content.

quiz.q: Match each setting to its documented default.
quiz.explain: These are the Python defaults in the docs checked 2026-10-13. Instrumentation became default-on in python-1.6.0, and content is off by default.

quiz.q: In .NET you wrap both the chat client and the agent with `UseOpenTelemetry` and sensitive data is on. What happens?
options: Traces are sampled twice as heavily
Prompts and responses appear on both spans, duplicating content
quiz.explain: Instrumenting both layers duplicates content on both spans when sensitive data is on, so pick one layer. The Harness wraps both layers by default.

flashcards.front: Which spans does Agent Framework emit?
flashcards.back: `invoke_agent <agent_name>`, `chat <model_name>` and `execute_tool <function_name>`, plus workflow, executor and edge spans.

flashcards.front: What changed in python-1.6.0 (2026-05-21) for telemetry?
flashcards.back: Instrumentation became on by default. Spans are created, but no exporter is installed and sensitive data stays off.

flashcards.front: Why can a default Python agent send nothing to Langfuse?
flashcards.back: The default OTLP protocol is gRPC and Langfuse accepts only OTLP over HTTP. Set the protocol to http.
